units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Just as he is going towards the door LORD CAVERSHAM enters from the smoking-room .
Well, sir? am I to wait attendance on you?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Considerably perplexed .
In a moment, father. Do excuse me.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: LORD CAVERSHAM goes back .
Well, remember my instructions, Phipps—into that room.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: LORD GORING goes into the smoking-room .
HAROLD, the footman shows MRS. CHEVELEY in .
Lamia-like , she is in green and silver .
She has a cloak of black satin , lined with dead rose-leaf silk .
What name, madam?
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: To PHIPPS, who advances towards her .
Is Lord Goring not here? I was told he was at home?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: His lordship is engaged at present with Lord Caversham, madam.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Turns a cold , glassy eye on HAROLD, who at once retires .
To herself .
How very filial!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: His lordship told me to ask you, madam, to be kind enough to wait in the drawing-room for him. His lordship will come to you there.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: With a look of surprise .
Lord Goring expects me?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Yes, madam.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Are you quite sure?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: His lordship told me that if a lady called I was to ask her to wait in the drawing-room.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Goes to the door of the drawing-room and opens it .
His lordship’s directions on the subject were very precise.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: To herself.
How thoughtful of him! To expect the unexpected shows a thoroughly modern intellect.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Goes towards the drawing-room and looks in .
Ugh! How dreary a bachelor’s drawing-room always looks. I shall have to alter all this.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: PHIPPS brings the lamp from the writing-table .
No, I don’t care for that lamp. It is far too glaring. Light some candles.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Replaces lamp .
Certainly, madam.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: I hope the candles have very becoming shades.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: We have had no complaints about them, madam, as yet.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Passes into the drawing-room and begins to light the candles .
To herself .
I wonder what woman he is waiting for to-night. It will be delightful to catch him. Men always look so silly when they are caught. And they are always being caught.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Looks about room and approaches the writing-table .
What a very interesting room! What a very interesting picture! Wonder what his correspondence is like.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Takes up letters .

Oh, what a very uninteresting correspondence! Bills and cards, debts and dowagers! Who on earth writes to him on pink paper? How silly to write on pink paper! It looks like the beginning of a middle-class romance. Romance should never begin with sentiment. It should begin with science and end with a settlement.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Puts letter down , then takes it up again .

I know that handwriting. That is Gertrude Chiltern’s. I remember it perfectly. The ten commandments in every stroke of the pen, and the moral law all over the page. Wonder what Gertrude is writing to him about? Something horrid about me, I suppose. How I detest that woman!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Reads it .
‘I trust you. I want you. I am coming to you. Gertrude.’ ‘I trust you. I want you. I am coming to you.’
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: A look of triumph comes over her face .
She is just about to steal the letter , when PHIPPS comes in .
